memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is so great and their sin so grievous that I will go down and see if what they have done is as bad as the outcry that has reached me. If not, I will know." - Gen 18:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks of "the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah." Behind the sin of those cities were victims - the oppressed, the abused, the wronged - whose cries had reached the ears of God. Sin is never merely private; it wounds real people, and their cries do not go unheard. God hears the outcry of the mistreated.

Then notice how God describes His response: "I will go down and see." Of course, God already knows everything. But this language shows us something about His justice - He does not act on rumour or hasty judgement. He is portrayed as investigating carefully, thoroughly, fairly. God's justice is never reckless or arbitrary.

This is deeply reassuring. We live in a world of hasty accusations, mob judgements, and injustice dressed up as righteousness. But God is not like that. He judges perfectly, with complete knowledge and perfect fairness. No one is ever wrongly condemned by God, and no genuine outcry is ever ignored.

For the oppressed, this is comfort: God hears your cry and will act justly. For all of us, it is a call to reflect His character - to judge fairly, to refuse hasty condemnation, to hear the cries of the wronged. "The Lord is a God of justice" (Isa 30:18), and one day "he will judge the world in righteousness" (Acts 17:31). We can trust the perfect Judge.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you trust God to judge the world's injustices perfectly and fairly?
- Are you quick to hasty judgement, or do you seek truth carefully like God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are the perfect Judge who hears every outcry and judges with complete fairness. Thank You that no injustice escapes You. Help me trust Your justice, and reflect Your fairness in how I judge others.
Amen.
